summary: Modified computePackageIdentity and computeWorkerPackageIdentities to accept an optional manifestPaths parameter. When provided AND non-empty, the identity is scoped to manifest-declared paths only — excluding auxiliary runtime/cache files (.npm/* logs with timestamps in filenames). Threaded the manifest through buildPackageCandidates and captureVerificationResult.

implementation_changes.change: Added optional manifestPaths parameter. When provided AND non-empty, filters snapshots to only those whose normalized path is in the manifest set. When undefined or empty, uses all snapshots (pre-G7-19G behavior).
Added optional manifestPaths parameter. Passes it through to computePackageIdentity for each worker.

Now passes requiredManifest to computePackageIdentity (line 675). This is the G7-19G fix: the candidate's identity is manifest-scoped, matching the captured verified identity (which is also manifest-scoped via captureVerificationResult).

Extracts the manifest from rt.acceptanceCriteria via extractManifestFromAcceptanceCriteria, passes it to computeWorkerPackageIdentities. This ensures the captured identity and the selection-time identity are BOTH manifest-scoped (consistent).

existing_tests_updated: tests/runtime/g7-19c-package-selection.test.ts — verifiedIds helper accepts optional manifest; Scenario 8 (extra non-required files) passes manifest to keep captured+candidate identities consistent

tests/runtime/g7-19d-content-binding.test.ts — verifiedIds helper accepts optional manifest; Scenario 3 (post-verification extra file) updated to use path-coverage check (the new detection mechanism for post-verification extra-file injection, since manifest-scoped identity no longer changes when extras are added)

guarantees_verified.1_identical_deliverables_different_cache: PASS — manifest-scoped identity excludes .npm/* cache files; two workers with identical manifest content but different .npm timestamps have the SAME manifest-scoped identity (only workerId differs in the canonical)
guarantees_verified.2_changed_deliverable_content_different_: PASS — manifest-scoped identity still changes when manifest file content changes
guarantees_verified.3_incomplete_manifests_rejected: PASS — assessPackageCompleteness unchanged; rejects missing manifest paths
guarantees_verified.4_unsafe_extra_files_rejected: PASS — assessPackageCompleteness unchanged; rejects unsafe paths (.., absolute, NUL bytes)
guarantees_verified.5_auxiliary_files_remain_visible: PASS — buildAggregatedRecords still includes all artifacts in the records; the .npm/* files are visible to consumers (not silently ignored); they're only excluded from the identity hash
guarantees_verified.6_content_hash_binding_preserved: PASS — captured identity (manifest-scoped) matches selection-time identity (manifest-scoped) when content unchanged; mismatch detected when content changes (G7-19D regression check)

remaining_limitations: When manifestPaths is undefined or empty (missions with no caller-supplied file-type acceptance criteria), the identity uses ALL snapshots (pre-G7-19G behavior). This is the only sensible default when there's no manifest to filter by — but it means the .npm-logs-alter-identity issue persists for missions without a manifest. In practice, the structural floor always produces file-type checks (one per produced artifact path), so the manifest will usually include all produced paths. The G7-19G fix specifically helps when the caller supplies a STRICTER manifest (e.g., only the 5 expected files, not the .npm cache).

Post-verification extra-file injection is now detected via the PATH-COVERAGE check (the extra's path is not in verifiedPaths), not the identity check (the extra doesn't change the manifest-scoped identity). This is a behavior change from G7-19D, which detected it via identity mismatch. The OUTCOME is the same (rejection), but the mechanism is different. The G7-19D Scenario 3 test was updated to reflect this.
